>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Tens of millions of people along the east coast are in the path of a major storm.
The forecast has already disrupted professional sports games, flights and concerts.
Now strong winds and heavy rain are moving into the region.
NPR's Amy Held reports the nor'easter is forecast to bring major flooding as it parks itself off the coast.
>> An unusually early season nor'easter is upending the weekend from the Carolinas to New England.
On Long Island in New York, Melissa Slavin says she's ready for 48 hours inside with her kids.
>> Applying extra groceries, preparing, rescheduling all the kids' sports.
>> Coastal flooding is forecast to be significant, widespread and repeated.
At the Jersey Shore...
>> Take this storm seriously.
>> Mike Mangan is mayor of Manasquan.
>> There's going to be a lot of water in the streets for a long time.
>> Part of the problem, the system is lingering, says meteorologist Frank Pereira.
>> It's going to kind of sit there for a day or two through the remainder of the weekend,
kind of looping around that area before it finally moves out early next week.
>> Tonight's moon is full, making for even higher tides and flooding.
Amy Held, NPR News.
>> President Trump is traveling to Tennessee for a college football game today.
NPR's Danielle Kurt Slavin reports it's a matchup of two southeastern conference powerhouses,
the University of Tennessee and the University of Texas.
>> The president has no other events on his schedule,
so it's unclear how much he will be in campaign mode with midterms just over a month away.
Solidly read, Tennessee has no battleground house, senate or governor's races,
though Texas' senate race is considered a toss-up.
Trump has worked to make sports a part of his brand this term,
holding a UFC match on the White House lawn and attending several other sporting events,
including the Super Bowl and the World Cup Final.
The university is offering half-price concessions, including alcohol,
from 9 to 10 a.m. to incentivize fans to get in early for the noon game,
which will have heightened security for the president's visit.
Danielle Kurt Slavin, NPR News, the White House.
♪♪
>> Pope Leo received a warm welcome when he arrived in Paris on Friday
as part of his four-day trip to France.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports crowds are gathering in the French capital
where the pontiff will celebrate mass.
>> The pope is holding a mass today at the Place de la Concorde
that is a symbol of the secular French Revolution,
and there's more than half a million people who will come out for it.
I'm heading there myself in the crowds
that are just going through the closed-off streets of Paris.
The pope's four-day trip includes two days in Paris,
and then he will go to the shrine site of Lourdes.
Then he will go to the eastern city of Mess,
where he will give a speech that European leaders are expected to attend.
>> That's NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reporting from Paris.
This is "NPR News in Washington."
Utah Valley University has released a report on the assassination of Charlie Kirk
showing lapses in security plans.
Caroline Ballard of member station KUER reports the conservative activist
was shot and killed on the school's campus last September.
>> The 157-page report by an independent investigator
stated that no one at UVU acted in bad faith
or with willful disregard to other's safety.
But while the university does have safety policies in place,
the report found some of them were "significantly inconsistent."
The school did not complete a formal security assessment
or have an event action plan,
and it deferred critical decisions to Kirk's organization, Turning Point USA,
including the choice to hold the event outdoors.
Kirk's family said they plan to sue UVU and the state over security failures.
Accused killer Tyler Robinson is set to stand trial for murder.
For "NPR News," I'm Caroline Ballard in Salt Lake City.
>> The federal appeals court has sided with the Pentagon in its fight
with the AI company, Anthropic.
The court upheld a decision to remove Anthropic's Claude technology
from military systems over national security concerns.
The dispute began when Anthropic refused to lift restrictions
on Claude's use in domestic surveillance and autonomous warfare.
A separate federal judge ruled last month
that another Pentagon effort to blacklist Anthropic was unlawful.
That ruling remains in place for now.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.
